sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains why the future redemption is compared to the Exodus, as the Exodus opened the channel for all subsequent redemptions, including the future one, just as it prepared for the giving of the Torah.

translations.translation: However, based on this, we must understand what is written: "As in the days of your exodus from the land of Egypt, I will show him wonders."
Why does the verse compare the wonders of the future redemption to the wonders that were in the days of your exodus from the land of Egypt?
And even more so, it is not understood
according to the opinion that we mention the Exodus from Egypt even in the days of Mashiach,
for seemingly,
since the revelations of the future will be vastly superior to the revelations that were in the Exodus from Egypt,
why will they mention the Exodus from Egypt even then?
And the explanation of this is known
(as explained in the discourse "Kimei Tzeischa" by my revered father-in-law, the Rebbe),
that in the redemption from Egypt, the entire concept of redemption was renewed, and the channel was opened for all redemptions
(from the exiles
that followed the exile of Egypt),
including the future redemption,
even though it will be a loftier redemption.
And this is analogous to the known idea that the Exodus from Egypt was a preparation for the giving of the Torah,
as it is written,
"When you bring the people out of Egypt, you will serve G-d on this mountain,"
for although the essence of redemption and freedom was specifically at the time of the giving of the Torah,
because before the giving of the Torah, the decree that "the upper ones shall not descend to the lower ones, and the lower ones shall not ascend to the upper ones" was still in effect,
it is therefore understood that until the giving of the Torah
(even after the Exodus from Egypt)
there was not yet the true redemption and freedom of the lower beings,
and nevertheless,
at the time of the redemption of the Exodus from Egypt, the power was given also for the redemption
(the nullification of the decree)
that occurred at the giving of the Torah,
so too is it regarding the future redemption,
that in the redemption of the Exodus from Egypt, the power was given also for the future redemption,
since at the time of the giving of the Torah there was already a semblance of the revelation of the future,
except that at the time of the giving of the Torah the revelation was only temporary, and in the future the revelation will be in a constant and eternal manner,
for the revelation then will not only be from the aspect of Above, as at the time of the giving of the Torah,
but also from the aspect of below,
for the creations will then be at the ultimate state of clarification and refinement, and will be vessels for the revelation of G-dliness,
to comprehend the knowledge of their Creator according to the capacity of man,
and this will be a complete place
for the indwelling of the Ein Sof light that is beyond the capacity of man.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that "days of your exodus" refers to all days from the first redemption until the future one, as each day's remembrance of the Exodus brings a higher level of liberation, culminating in the ultimate redemption through Mashiach.

translations.translation: And this is also the meaning of "As in the days of your exodus from the land of Egypt,"
"days" in the plural,
for all the days from the days of the first redemption from the exile of Egypt until the future redemption, speedily in our days, are the "days of your exodus from the land of Egypt,"
as explained in the discourse there.
That is to say,
that in the Exodus from Egypt, the channel was opened also for the future redemption,
the order of this is,
that on each and every day
(from the time of the Exodus from Egypt until the future redemption)
the concept of the Exodus from Egypt occurs in a more elevated manner,
until the ultimate elevation in this regard in the future redemption.
And the concept is,
behold, our sages said,
"In every generation and every day,
a person is obligated to see himself as if he himself went out
from Egypt."
For on each and every day there must be a going out from Egypt,
and specifically during the time of Kriyas Shema,
as the Alter Rebbe wrote,
that the reason they instituted the passage of the Exodus from Egypt specifically during Kriyas Shema is because they
(Kriyas Shema and the Exodus from Egypt)
are one thing,
and this concept
(that in Kriyas Shema there must be the service of the Exodus from Egypt)
applies also to the evening Kriyas Shema,
and as the Rambam wrote,
that the reason we read the passage of Tzitzis also in the evening Kriyas Shema,
even though the mitzvah of Tzitzis is not practiced at night,
is because it contains the remembrance of the Exodus from Egypt.
And this is "As in the days of your exodus from the land of Egypt,"
"days" in the plural,
even though the Exodus from Egypt was on one day,
for by mentioning the Exodus from Egypt every day
(which occurred the first time,
on one day)
behold, through this it becomes "days of your exodus from the land of Egypt," "days" in the plural,
that on each and every day they go out from more elevated constraints and limitations,
and one places oneself in a state of "and you shall burst forth" beyond measure and limitation,
until they come to the bursting forth in ultimate perfection in the true and complete redemption through our righteous Mashiach, about whom it is written,
"The one who breaks through has gone up before them."
For this is why Mashiach is a son of Dovid,
and also the sign of Mashiach is that he is engrossed in Torah and fulfills mitzvos like Dovid his father, etc., and wages the wars of G-d,
for Dovid is from the children of Peretz,
about whom it is written,
"What a breach you have made for yourself! A breach,"
the breaking through of all barriers, measures, and limitations.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the daily service from the beginning of the day (Mitzrayim/constriction) through the stages of subjugation and transformation mirrors the process from the Exodus to the future redemption, where even evil is transformed to good.

translations.translation: And behold, this order of redemption
[which begins from the simple Exodus from Egypt,
and continues through the service of remembering the Exodus from Egypt every day until the complete redemption through "the one who breaks through has gone up before us"]
has its parallel on each and every day.
For behold, at the beginning of the day, before prayer, a person is in Egypt,
in the constraints and limitations of the body,
and as it is written,
"Cease from man, whose soul is in his nostrils, for in what is he to be considered?"
Do not read it as "bameh" (in what) but rather "bamah" (a high place),
that at the beginning of the day, the soul is only in his nostrils and does not spread throughout the body, therefore he is considered then like a "bamah,"
which is the strength of the constraints and limitations of the body's materiality.
Therefore, the beginning of the service is in the aspect of subjugation,
where one overcomes the materiality of the body and the animal soul and the side of evil,
until one effects that even the body and the animal soul answer "amen" against their will and assist in serving G-d,
but even this is only in the manner of subjugation.
Until afterwards one comes to the aspect of transformation,
and within this itself, it is initially in the manner of "and my heart is hollow within me,"
and afterwards one reaches "and you shall love the L-rd your G-d with all your heart, with both your inclinations,"
that even the evil inclination itself is turned to good,
similar to complete repentance
(repentance out of love)
where intentional sins become like merits,
and even become actual merits.
For these two concepts that occur each day
(subjugation and transformation)
are parallel to the redemption of the Exodus from Egypt and the future redemption.
For regarding the Exodus from Egypt it is written, "for the people fled,"
that evil was at its peak and they needed to flee from evil,
the aspect of subjugation.
And in the future it will be, "and I will remove the spirit of impurity from the land"
(similar to "and my heart is hollow within me"),
and moreover, even evil itself will be turned to good
(similar to "with all your heart, with both your inclinations"),
and as it is written,
"For then I will turn to the peoples a pure language, that they may all call upon the name of G-d, to serve Him with one accord,"
that even the nations themselves will turn to serve Him, blessed be He,
"and strangers will stand and pasture your flocks."
And similarly with animals,
"and I will cause evil beasts to cease from the land,"
meaning I will cause them to cease from harming,
for although even then the existence of evil beasts will remain, nevertheless they will not harm,
and moreover, they will assist and serve the service of G-d,
and as it is written,
"and the wolf will dwell with the lamb, etc., and the lion like an ox, etc.,"
that there will be benefit from the wolf as from the lamb, and from the lion as from the ox,
and even the serpent
(the viper,
the asp)
will be a great luminary,
meaning not only will the serpent also serve the service of G-d,
but moreover,
its service will be in a manner of greatness,
a great luminary.
